A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WaltzRL. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety, overrefusal and general-capability evaluations, reward and training ablations, training curves and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on freezing the conversation agent, replacing DIR and restricting trajectory sampling.

M1.justification: The collaborative protocol, DIR, reward conditioning, mixed trajectory sampling, policy updates and two-stage training remain unchanged. The new experiments test ablated variants of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain WildJailbreak and OR-Bench training data and the same safety, overrefusal and general-capability evaluation suites. The added ablations reuse existing datasets; adaptive-attack evaluation is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same baselines, including Llama Guard 4, single-model RL and oracle label-converted feedback. New Tables 5, 6 and 8 add internal comparison variants: a frozen conversation agent, DIR replaced with an outcome reward, and training with only one trajectory type.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce controls that freeze the conversation agent throughout both training stages, replace DIR with the next-response outcome reward, or restrict sampling to one trajectory type. They also introduce an aggregate F1 metric. Previously documented model sizes, data splits and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's reward-conditioning and stage-removal analyses, v2 directly tests three central design choices: continued agent co-training, improvement reward versus outcome reward, and mixed trajectory sampling (Tables 5, 6 and 8). This substantially expands component-level validation. Existing training curves and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new ablation tables continue reporting point estimates, and the retained training plots have unchanged uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially extends quantitative component comparisons while retaining all previous results. The frozen-agent variant reports average ASR/ORR of 5.1%/14.2%, versus WaltzRL's 3.7%/7.6%. DIR replacement reports 8.4%/6.7%, revealing worse safety but less overrefusal. Single-trajectory variants report F1 scores of 93.8% and 92.4%, versus 94.3% for mixed sampling (Tables 5, 6 and 8).

T1.justification: The new table captions define a task-specific F1 aggregate as the harmonic mean of 1-average ASR and 1-average ORR. The game formulation, reward equations and policy-gradient derivation are unchanged; no proofs or theoretical guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about collaborative alignment, DIR, reduced unsafe responses and overrefusal, and preserved general capabilities. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that evaluation uses static adversarial prompts and leaves stronger adaptive attacks untested (Appendix F). It also interprets the new ablations as evidence for co-training, DIR and mixed sampling. Existing limitations concerning English data and one feedback round remain.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain unchanged: training sample counts, hyperparameters, RL frameworks, WildGuard judging, evaluation tools and access links, and both system prompts. The new ablation descriptions specify experimental interventions without additional implementation or resource disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nasr et al. on adaptive attacks and Zhang et al.'s Jailbreak Distillation to support the new evaluation limitation. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against safeguards and competitive multi-agent approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: additional ablation paragraphs, a new Appendix E, a latency footnote, cross-reference updates and author-affiliation/correspondence edits. Later appendices are renumbered, while the main narrative remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact ablation tables with an F1 column, renumbers the former Table 5 as Table 7, and places the unchanged Figures 3 and 4 together on one appendix page. Surrounding text reflows, but existing plots and the overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: The new controls strengthen evidence for the existing design, especially DIR versus an outcome reward and co-training versus continued freezing. The explicit static-attack limitation also clarifies applicability. These are focused improvements: uncertainty remains unreported, and Table 6 supports an aggregate benefit with a safety/overrefusal tradeoff, rather than uniform superiority.
